program_meta.program_name: Ph.D. in Computer Science, College of Computing (admits into the School of Computer Science, School of Interactive Computing, or School of Computational Science & Engineering). Sibling programs that hire the same advisors: Ph.D. in Machine Learning (interdisciplinary, run through ML@GT), Ph.D. in Computational Science & Engineering, Ph.D. in Robotics, Ph.D. in Electrical & Computer Engineering (ECE), Ph.D. in Bioengineering / Coulter BME (joint Georgia Tech + Emory). The M.S. in Computer Science is a SEPARATE application from the Ph.D. - verbatim from the CoC page: '*Note that our Master's (M.S.) program is separate from our Ph.D. program. If the eventual degree you seek is a Ph.D., you will need to apply directly to the doctoral program.'

program_meta.english_test: GEORGIA TECH'S BAR IS UNUSUALLY HIGH AND THE POLICY CHANGES EXACTLY FOR AKSHAT'S CYCLE. (1) INSTITUTE MINIMUM (grad.gatech.edu/english-proficiency): TOEFL iBT 90+ on the pre-Jan-2026 0-120 scale, or 4.5+ on the new post-Jan-2026 1-6 scale (section minimums old scale 19+; new scale Reading >=4, Listening >=4, Writing >=4, Speaking >=3.5). IELTS Academic 7.0 overall with Reading >=6.5, Listening >=6.5, Speaking >=6.5, Writing >=5.5. NOT ACCEPTED: TOEFL Essentials, IELTS General Training, Duolingo, PTE. Scores valid two years. (2) COLLEGE OF COMPUTING Ph.D. CS REQUIRES HIGHER - verbatim: 'The required minimum is 100 on the older scale, and 5.0 on the new scale effective January 2026. We will also accept IELTS beginning in Spring 2020. A minimum overall score of 7.5 is required, with minimum section scores as follows: Reading 6.5, Listening 6.5, Speaking 6.5, Writing 5.5.' So plan for TOEFL 100 / new-scale 5.0, or IELTS 7.5. (3) INDIA EXEMPTION: there is NO blanket country exemption for India, and 'Effective starting with Fall 2027 admission, citizenship alone will no longer be sufficient to satisfy Georgia Tech's English language proficiency requirement.' HOWEVER the medium-of-instruction pathway applies - verbatim FAQ: 'My university's language of instruction was English, but my country is not on the approved country pathway list. Do I need a test? No. If English was the language of instruction for your degree program, you may satisfy the English proficiency requirement by providing documentation from your institution confirming this. Acceptable documentation may include: a transcript notation, institutional letter, or Medium of Instruction certificate.' and 'My transcript says "English" as the language of instruction. Is that sufficient? Yes.' ACTION: get an MoI certificate / transcript notation from Manipal Institute of Technology Bengaluru early. Note the CoC page separately says TOEFL 'is required for candidates whose native language is not English and who have not studied in the United States for at least one year' - the CoC and Institute wordings are not perfectly aligned, so confirm with the CoC graduate office that the MoI route is accepted for the Ph.D. CS program specifically.

program_meta.advisor_model: Program-level admission with strong advisor influence, plus a separate 'home unit' concept that is unusual and matters. Best verbatim explanation, from Pan Li (ECE/ML@GT): 'Note that at Georgia Tech., it is common to have two advisors co-advise you. If you plan to apply for a Ph.D. position and select me as the unique advisor, you may apply through the machine learning program, and the ECE program, and select ECE as your home unit. The home unit at Georgia Tech. is not much related to the program/the degree but related to where the advisor is. You may also join other programs such as the CS program or the ISYE program and still would like to work with me. In these cases, I may work as a co-advisor of you and feel free to reach out to me and let me know who you also plan to work with in those programs.' Zsolt Kira (Interactive Computing) puts it as: 'Follow the application process of the college/school you are applying to. I am in the School of Interactive Computing under the College of Computing, and hire from several Ph.D. programs including machine learning (ML) and robotics. Mention my name in your application if you are interested in the lab.' PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE FOR AKSHAT: which school a professor sits in determines which Ph.D. program can admit him, so he may need to apply to CS Ph.D. and ML Ph.D. (and possibly ECE Ph.D.) to cover his shortlist - AlRegib and Pan Li are ECE, not College of Computing.
program_meta.ms_research_access: Yes for lab work, but funding is worse and the application is separate. Verbatim from CoC: 'Ph.D. candidates are typically offered a research or teaching assistantship which includes a stipend and tuition remission. The Master's program does not offer financial aid to the majority of students. Aid will be based on qualifications for the program, not need.' Individual labs do take M.S. students: Kira's lab, verbatim - 'M.S. & undergraduate students: Please fill out the interest form below and we will get back to you. Do this relatively early, before the subsequent semester starts.' Pan Li's group: 'Our team also provides some short-term research opportunities (approximately half a year to a year) for undergraduates and master's students... Excellent students can receive remuneration!' Given the PhD-primary strategy, the M.S. route at GT is a weak fallback (unfunded).

faculty.department: School of Interactive Computing, College of Computing; Associate Director, Machine Learning Center at Georgia Tech (ML@GT)
faculty.lab: Robotics Perception and Learning (RIPL), CODA S1181B
faculty.research_areas: Semi-supervised learning and pseudo-labelling (teacher-student), open-world / generalized category discovery, weakly-supervised learning, robust fine-tuning of foundation models, out-of-distribution generalization, calibration, continual learning, diffusion features as representations, embodied AI / vision-language-action models
faculty.why_match: Akshat's lumbar-spine MRI pipeline - teacher U-Net trained on 54 labelled images reaching 0.735 mIoU, then confidence-filtered pseudo-labels lifting a student to 0.816 mIoU (+8.1 absolute points), with unfiltered students stuck at 0.737-0.741 - is the medical-segmentation instance of exactly the mechanism Kira formalised in 'Unbiased Teacher v2: Semi-supervised Object Detection for Anchor-free and Anchor-based Detectors' (CVPR 2022), where the whole gain comes from how the teacher's pseudo-labels are thresholded and debiased. Second, Akshat's DDPM-pretraining result - a frozen diffusion encoder retained 86.9% of the fine-tuned liver Dice but fell BELOW a random-init baseline for kidney (0.654 vs 0.899) - is a concrete negative result against the general claim in Kira's 'Pre-trained Text-to-Image Diffusion Models Are Versatile Representation Learners for Control' (NeurIPS 2024) that diffusion representations transfer broadly; that per-structure asymmetry is a research question Kira's lab is equipped to take seriously.
faculty.key_paper_1: Unbiased Teacher v2: Semi-supervised Object Detection for Anchor-free and Anchor-based Detectors, CVPR, 2022 (see also Unbiased Teacher, ICLR 2021, and Open-Set Semi-Supervised Object Detection, ECCV 2022, oral)
faculty.key_paper_2: Pre-trained Text-to-Image Diffusion Models Are Versatile Representation Learners for Control, NeurIPS, 2024 (see also Diffuse, Attend, and Segment: Unsupervised Zero-Shot Segmentation using Stable Diffusion, CVPR 2024)
faculty.taking_students: Yes. Homepage (checked 2026-08-28): 'I am always looking for strong Ph.D. students and collaborators in machine learning, perception, and robotics.' Join page: 'I tend to accept one or two Ph.D. students every year in machine learning for perception and robotics.'

I am in the School of Interactive Computing under the College of Computing, and hire from several Ph.D. programs including machine learning (ML) and robotics. Mention my name in your application if you are interested in the lab.' VERBATIM, external students: 'External students / interns - I am not currently looking for external visiting researchers or interns. If you are not at Georgia Tech and not applying for a post-doc, the best way to work with me is by applying to the school (see above).' Contact me many weeks before the semester starts - opportunities fill up quickly.' INTERPRETATION FOR AKSHAT: do not cold-email; name him explicitly in the SOP and in the application's faculty-selection field.
faculty.email: zkira at gatech dot edu (obfuscated on his site; do not use for a cold application email per policy above)
faculty.email_angle: Not an email target. In the SOP: 'Unbiased Teacher v2 argues the gain lives in how pseudo-labels are filtered, not in the architecture; on 54 labelled lumbar-spine MRIs I found the same thing, and also that thresholds calibrated on 5 reference images match those calibrated on 304 - I want to know how far that calibration-efficiency goes.'
faculty.notes: STRONGEST single fit at Georgia Tech, but read the drift: the lab's 2025-2026 output (news feed and publication list) is heavily vision-language-action models, embodied AI, memory for agents, and robust fine-tuning of VLMs. The semi-supervised / pseudo-labelling / category-discovery core is 2021-2023 with a live 2025 tail ('Contextual Self-paced Learning for Weakly Supervised Spatio-Temporal Video Grounding', ICLR 2025; 'When Domain Generalization meets Generalized Category Discovery', CVPR 2025). Frame the pitch as label efficiency and representation transfer for a fundamental-capability question, not as medical imaging. He is ML@GT Associate Director, so both the CS Ph.D. and the ML Ph.D. are viable routes to him.

faculty.department: School of Electrical and Computer Engineering (College of Engineering) - NOT the College of Computing. Faculty member of the Center for Signal and Information Processing (CSIP); Director, Center for Energy and Geo Processing (CeGP); listed in the ML@GT directory.
faculty.lab: OLIVES - Omni Lab for Intelligent Visual Engineering and Science, 777 Atlantic Dr. NW
faculty.research_areas: Label-efficient and human-in-the-loop learning, active learning / active prompting, uncertainty estimation and calibration, self-supervised learning, robustness and domain shift, explainability, applications in medical imaging (ophthalmology/OCT), seismic interpretation, and video
faculty.why_match: Akshat's spine-MRI study swept confidence thresholding against MC-dropout uncertainty for pseudo-label filtering and produced a genuine negative result - MC-dropout was merely comparable (0.791-0.792 mIoU) and COMBINING the two signals added nothing - which is precisely the 'which disagreement signal actually earns you an annotation' question OLIVES attacks in 'BALD-SAM: Disagreement-Based Active Prompting in Interactive Segmentation' (2026). Separately, Akshat's HiME imposes hierarchy at the output by construction (per-level conditional sigmoids composed by the chain rule, upward-closed prediction sets, ~0.01% parameter overhead, 95.8% decision-level accuracy on Galaxy Zoo 2's 239,573 images / 37 classes / 4 levels); AlRegib's group instead tries to EXPLOIT hierarchy that emerges inside self-supervised representations in 'HEX: Hierarchical Emergence Exploitation in Self-Supervised Algorithms' (WACV 2025). Imposed-vs-emergent hierarchy is a directly shared, publishable disagreement.
faculty.key_paper_1: HEX: Hierarchical Emergence Exploitation in Self-Supervised Algorithms, IEEE/CVF WACV, 2025 (K. Kokilepersaud, S. Kim, M. Prabhushankar, G. AlRegib)
faculty.key_paper_2: Scale-Aware Self-Supervised Learning for Segmentation of Small and Sparse Structures, ICASSP, 2026 (J. Quesada, G. AlRegib). See also BALD-SAM: Disagreement-Based Active Prompting in Interactive Segmentation (arXiv 2603.10828, submitted to IEEE Access Mar 2026) and FedKPer: Tackling Generalization and Personalization in Medical Federated Learning via Knowledge Personalization (ICIP 2026).
faculty.taking_students: Unstated. No statement about admitting students in the current cycle was found on the lab site, the bio page, or the contact page (checked 2026-08-28). The group is large and is publishing at a high rate into 2026 (multiple ICIP 2026, ICML 2026, ICASSP 2026, WACV 2026 papers), which is weak positive evidence.
faculty.contact_policy: not stated. The entire Contact page reads, VERBATIM: 'Ghassan AlRegib / Tel: +1 404 894 7005 / Email: alregib@gatech.edu (remove ^ after adding last name) / 777 Atlantic Dr. NW, Atlanta, GA 30332-0250, U.S.A.' There is no instruction for or against prospective-student email anywhere on the lab site. Absence of a prohibition - a short, specific email is defensible.
faculty.email_angle: 'HEX exploits hierarchy that emerges inside an SSL representation; HiME instead makes hierarchy a decoding constraint so violations are impossible by construction - and I found the constraint is free under a fine-tuned encoder (0.952) but costs accuracy under a frozen one (0.858 vs 0.888 flat). I would like to know which regime your emergent hierarchy lives in.'

To be advised by him Akshat would most naturally apply to the ECE Ph.D. or the ML Ph.D. with ECE as home unit - the CS Ph.D. application alone may not reach him. faculty.rank: Associate Professor (listed on the CoC profile as 'Edenfield Early-Career Associate Professor'; his own site says 'James Edenfield Associate Professor'). Also an Amazon Scholar.
faculty.department: School of Computational Science and Engineering, College of Computing; affiliated with IDEaS and ML@GT. Office CODA E1358B.
faculty.lab: Not separately named on his site; group listed as ~9 current Ph.D. students
faculty.research_areas: Stated on his Georgia Tech profile: 'enable machines to understand text data in more label-efficient and robust way in open-world settings... weakly-supervised learning, out-of-distribution generalization, interpretable machine learning'. Current 2025-2026 output: LLM agents, inference-time search and planning, post-training, uncertainty quantification, label-noise refinement, AI for scientific discovery.
faculty.why_match: Akshat's A-PDF work refuses to trust the generator's own discriminator and instead scores cWGAN-GP samples against the class-proportion distribution of real masks, keeping only 33.7% (Mahalanobis) / 35.1% (kNN) of 5,000 generated images versus 86% under a naive per-class range filter - i.e. a post-hoc quality filter over machine-produced supervision. Chao Zhang's 'Calibrating Pre-trained Language Classifiers on LLM-generated Noisy Labels via Iterative Refinement' (KDD 2025) is the identical problem stated in text: labels produced by a model are systematically wrong and must be refined and recalibrated rather than consumed. And Akshat's habit of benchmarking uncertainty estimators against each other rather than assuming one works (thresholding vs MC-dropout, and finding the combination adds nothing) is the same move as 'MUBen: Benchmarking the Uncertainty of Pre-Trained Models for Molecular Property Prediction' (TMLR 2024).
faculty.key_paper_1: Calibrating Pre-trained Language Classifiers on LLM-generated Noisy Labels via Iterative Refinement, ACM SIGKDD (KDD), 2025 (L. Ye, A. Shah, C. Zhang, S. Chava)
faculty.key_paper_2: MUBen: Benchmarking the Uncertainty of Pre-Trained Models for Molecular Property Prediction, TMLR, 2024. See also Language Model Uncertainty Quantification with Attention Chain, COLM 2025.
faculty.taking_students: Yes. VERBATIM (site last updated June 2026): 'Prospective students: I am always looking for strong and motivated students to join our group.'
faculty.contact_policy: VERBATIM: 'Prospective students: I am always looking for strong and motivated students to join our group. If you are interested in working with me, you can either email me or fill out this form.' (The form is https://forms.gle/Locv9n73nKrfN8Ci9.) This is an EXPLICIT OPEN DOOR - one of only two on this list. Do both: fill the form and send a short email.
faculty.email_angle: 'Your KDD 2025 paper refines LLM-generated noisy labels rather than trusting them; I built the image-side version - a post-hoc Mahalanobis/kNN filter that scores cWGAN-GP samples against the class-proportion statistics of real masks and discards two-thirds of them - and I want to work on what makes a machine-produced label worth keeping.'
faculty.notes: IMPORTANT DRIFT: his Georgia Tech profile still describes the weak-supervision / label-efficiency agenda, but his own homepage research section (updated June 2026) has been entirely rewritten around LLM agents on long-horizon tasks, inference-time search, post-training, and AI for chemistry/materials. The label-noise and uncertainty thread survives (KDD 2025, COLM 2025, TMLR 2024) but is no longer the centre of the lab. Do NOT pitch him medical image segmentation. Pitch data quality, label noise, and uncertainty-guided selection under a limited evaluation budget - his 'uncertainty-guided selection that routes evaluation budget toward the most informative candidates' framing is almost word-for-word active learning. Awards: NSF CAREER 2022, GT CoC Outstanding Junior Faculty 2024. Vertical: School of CSE, so the CS Ph.D. and ML Ph.D. both reach him.

faculty.rank: Associate Professor (tenured March 2026); also a visiting faculty researcher at Google Research since May 2026
faculty.department: School of Electrical and Computer Engineering (Digital Signal Processing technical interest group) - NOT the College of Computing. Office CODA S1219.
faculty.research_areas: Machine learning on graphs, structural representation and positional encodings, geometric deep learning and symmetry-respecting architectures, graph domain adaptation and distribution shift, diffusion models for structured scientific data, privacy/unlearning, graph-augmented LLMs
faculty.why_match: HiME's whole claim is that a structural constraint belongs in the decoding rule rather than in a post-hoc repair step: per-level conditional sigmoids composed by the chain rule make a child's probability unable to exceed its parent's, so the prediction set is upward-closed by construction, at ~38K parameters (~0.01% overhead) and verified across five backbones. Pan Li's 'Improving Graph Neural Networks on Multi-node Tasks with Labeling Tricks' (JMLR 2025) is the same species of argument - it formalises when injecting structure (including partial-order labeling tricks) into the input/representation buys expressiveness that the architecture cannot otherwise reach. PARTIAL because his objects are graphs and scientific data, not taxonomic image labels, and he has no label-efficiency or medical-imaging line.
faculty.key_paper_1: Improving Graph Neural Networks on Multi-node Tasks with Labeling Tricks, JMLR, 2025 (X. Zhang, M. Zhang, P. Li)
faculty.key_paper_2: Pairwise Alignment Improves Graph Domain Adaptation, ICML, 2024 (spotlight). See also Structural Alignment Improves Graph Test-Time Adaptation, ICLR 2026.
faculty.taking_students: Yes. VERBATIM: 'I keep looking for passionate Ph.D. students and I plan to hire 1-2 Ph.D. students every year. And currently, the team has one postdoc opening.' And: 'Every year, I expect to hire 1-2 Ph.D. students.'

I would like to understand where that boundary actually sits.'
faculty.notes: HIGHEST-VALUE ADMINISTRATIVE SOURCE on this list - his homepage is the clearest public explanation of Georgia Tech's home-unit / co-advising model (quoted in program_meta.advisor_model). ECE home unit, so reachable via the ML Ph.D. or the ECE Ph.D.; he explicitly says CS-program students can still work with him as a co-advisee. Caveats: (a) his 2025-2026 output has swung strongly toward LLMs, unlearning, privacy and agent reasoning; (b) his stated bar includes C/C++ systems-level coding, which Akshat should evidence via the ROS 2 / 56 FPS real-time perception work rather than the medical-imaging papers; (c) he explicitly penalises template emails, so any email must be specific. Wife Cong Hao is also GT ECE (efficient hardware/AI) - a possible co-advisor pairing for the efficiency interest.

faculty.rank: Assistant Professor; concurrently Senior Staff Research Scientist at Google DeepMind (since Mar 2023)
faculty.department: School of Computational Science and Engineering, College of Computing. Office CODA E1342A.
faculty.lab: Not separately named; 5 current Georgia Tech CSE Ph.D. students listed
faculty.research_areas: Generative models as representation learners, spectral/representation-based reinforcement learning, diffusion policies and diffusion representations, non-contrastive representation learning, LLM agents for ML engineering, efficient language-image pretraining
faculty.why_match: Akshat's diffusion work pretrained a DDPM on unlabelled abdominal CT and then transferred the encoder, getting liver Dice 0.751 -> 0.928 and a frozen encoder that retained 86.9% of fine-tuned liver performance while FAILING for kidney (0.654 vs a 0.899 random-init baseline) - the open question being what a denoiser's internal features actually encode and for which structures. Bo Dai's 'Diffusion Spectral Representation for Reinforcement Learning' (NeurIPS 2024) is built on the same premise, extracting a usable representation from a diffusion model instead of sampling from it, and 'Representation Learning via Non-Contrastive Mutual Information' (AISTATS 2026, spotlight) asks what a pretext objective actually teaches. PARTIAL because his testbeds are control/RL and language, never medical images, and no label-efficiency or segmentation line exists in the group.
faculty.key_paper_1: Diffusion Spectral Representation for Reinforcement Learning, NeurIPS, 2024 (D. Shribak, C.-X. Gao, Y. Li, C. Xiao, B. Dai)
faculty.key_paper_2: Representation Learning via Non-Contrastive Mutual Information, AISTATS, 2026 (Spotlight). See also Efficient Online Reinforcement Learning for Diffusion Policy, ICML 2025.

faculty.notes: Split appointment with Google DeepMind - factor that into expected availability. Also worth noting he co-authors constantly with Chao Zhang (MLE-Dojo NeurIPS 2025, MLE-Smith ICLR 2026, BBox-Adapter ICML 2024, AdaPlanner NeurIPS 2023), so a Chao Zhang + Bo Dai co-advising pairing at the School of CSE is a realistic and coherent ask. He teaches CX 4240 and CSE 6243. Match rated Partial rather than Close because the shared object is 'diffusion representations' in the abstract only; no shared problem domain, no shared evaluation setting.

faculty.rank: Associate Professor; Co-Director, Center for Advancing Responsible Computing (CARE)
faculty.department: School of Computer Science, College of Computing; ML@GT
faculty.lab: Efficient and Intelligent Computing (EIC) Lab, 266 Ferst Dr NW
faculty.research_areas: Efficient machine learning via cross-layer innovation - efficient AI algorithms, hardware accelerators, AI chip design; efficient inference and on-device AI; data-mixture selection for pretraining; 3D/NeRF acceleration; LLM efficiency
faculty.why_match: Akshat's polyp study is the cleanest data-centric ablation he has: architecture held FIXED, preprocessing varied, contribution measured across three backbones (+0.0453 U-Net, +0.0579 ResU-Net, +0.0226 Attention U-Net) with the gain SHRINKING as the backbone strengthens - a direct measurement of data intervention substituting for representational capacity.
